correctness.rationale: Direct substitution into the actual AdaMod bias-corrected source recurrence gives \(x_1/r=2d-1\) and the exact two-state sign-alternating map. Its rational derivative bounds prove a uniform \(24/25\) contraction on an invariant square for the entire stated interval; this proves infinite-time convergence without relying on a finite iteration trace. The positive-moment continuation uses an explicit four-dimensional signed state, tail fixed point, weighted norm contraction at zero moments, continuous persistence on a compact ball, source finite-entry continuity, and summably decaying bias-correction errors. Standalone exact-rational checks and recurrence replay are provided.

value.rationale: AdaMod was motivated as an adaptive learning-rate safeguard. The exact analysis isolates a failure not visible from the known first-step attenuation: its cap is active at startup and yields strict initial objective decrease, yet the coupled memory dynamics converge to a persistent nonzero error on the simplest strongly convex objective. An open parameter rectangle, uniform explicit geometric certificate, and robustness to positive moment decays show the behavior is structural rather than a one-off algebraic curiosity. This is a motivated limit of rate-smoothing safety, with an exact boundary between transient progress and asymptotic stationarity under its defined assumptions.
